items.title: Arnold Loyacano Interview, 1956-09-29
items.q: Bill Lambert on drums, and Steve Brown on bass, and myself on guitar. That was a band.

ctx.x: flannel under shirt too. That's true. In the summertime. Well now, uh, what's, uh, the outfit that you remember, uh, that you played with in your audience before you left here?

Yeah, before you left there? Oh, well, I was working with Tommy Brown then. Uh, Tommy Brown in a regular outfit. Yeah, I was playing guitar with him. Uh, huh. You see? They had, uh, Gus Miller on clarinet, Raymond Lopez on trumpet, Tommy Brown on trombone, Bill Lambert on drums, and Steve Brown on bass, and myself on guitar. That was a band. Well, those days, Tommy had cut deeply into Jack Lane, uh, as far as work is concerned. We had quite a bit of work, and we got more money that, uh, Tommy Brown than we did…
a dollar and a half all day long at Millenburg or West End. What about baseball games? You all played out the Ironman Park?

items.title: Steve "Ted" Brown Interview, 1958-04-22
items.q: He took my place when I left, when I left the band in 1913. He took my place and played from then on.

ctx.x: Well, which Lai Canna was it that you mentioned, uh? Arnold Lai Canna. Arnold, huh? He went up to, with Tom.

Oh, I see. He took my place when I left, when I left the band in 1913. He took my place and played from then on. Uh, played in Chicago and went to New York with them. And, uh, the going got pretty rough in New York, I understand, for Tom and them. And, uh, Lai Canna and Lambert and Shields, I think, beat it out of New York. One other question. What did you call that band down here? What was the name of it? Well, we, uh, we called it just Brown's Band. Brown's Band. And sometimes some people would put across on…
What pieces did you play then? Do you remember some of the numbers?
